newsitem.title: INDIA: India's BJP wants all of Kashmir in Delhi's hands.
newsitem.headline: India's BJP wants all of Kashmir in Delhi's hands.

text.p: India's main opposition Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Tuesday urged the government to seek the reunification of Kashmir under New Delhi's control in talks with Pakistan.

The Hindu nationalist party noted in a statement that Indian and Pakistani negotiators agreed in Islamabad in talks that ended on Monday to discuss all outstanding issues including Jammu and Kashmir state.
Pakistan has controlled one third of the Kashmir region since the two nations fought their first of three wars shortly after winning independence from Britain in 1947.
The BJP said the basis for any discussion with Pakistan over Jammu and Kashmir was a resolution that the Indian parliament unanimously passed in 1994.
"More specifically it means that during the talks on Jammu and Kashmir, the Indian side must seek the return of those portions of the state which were occupied by Pakistan in 1947-48," the BJP said.

The right-wing party, which held power for 12 days last May before failing to win enough support to survive a confidence motion, said the talks must be preceded by "a marked decrease in terrorism and other Pakistani-sponsored activities in Kashmir".

Pakistan denies India's accusations that it arms and trains guerrillas fighting New Delhi's rule in Jammu and Kashmir. Police and hospital officials say more than 20,000 people have died since the separatist revolt erupted in 1990.
The BJP welcomed the two sides' agreement to prevent hostile propaganda and provocative action against each other.
"It is to be hoped that Pakistan would abide by this agreement," the party said. "It should not be that this turns out to be a unilateral gesture by India as until now."
